Adventure threat rumor source reconstruction, PE 53.16
=====================================================

These are native source records extracted from the two configured executable
images in data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. They are not simulated outputs.
The .asm files contain the complete owning PE unwind ranges; packed trailing
switch bytes are represented as data, with decoded selections in
native-switches.tsv. image-sources.json identifies each image and function.

reference threat speech:      0x1406878f0..0x140688fa6
classic threat speech:        0x140685310..0x1406869c6
reference delegated details:  0x14065bfb0..0x14065e928
classic delegated details:    0x1406599d0..0x14065c348
reference site location:      0x140690060..0x140690b3a
classic site location:        0x14068da80..0x14068e55a
reference family formatter:   0x14075a580..0x14075ad31
classic family formatter:     0x140757fa0..0x140758751
reference cardinal formatter: 0x14052e360..0x14052eb6c
classic cardinal formatter:   0x14052bd80..0x14052c58c
reference English name:       0x140a946e0..0x140a94ea2
classic English name:         0x140a91760..0x140a91f22
reference stolen item noun:   0x140a82c10..0x140a882fc
classic stolen item noun:     0x140a7fc90..0x140a8537c

All coordinates below use the reference image. The corresponding classic
owners are saved in full. No game process was started, manipulated or read.

1. Speech owner and delegation
-----------------------------

threat_speech(speaker, threat, output, audience/context, ...):
    Resolve target historical figure and shared speech context.
    Classify the figure's race/caste, traits, and relations to the speaker's
    entity: local threat, known foe, military adversary, transformed creature,
    nature beast, underworld beast, wilderness creature or night creature.
    Select a complete opening sentence from the literal operands, not from
    isolated words. All selected opening operands are in native-literals.tsv.
    Append the identity introduction:
        Seek this place if you wish to confront {identity}.
        This insidious evil is {identity}.
        Seek this place if you hunt {identity}.
        The creature is {identity}.
    Identity is assembled by the complete selection below; the name and
    selected RAW fields can also be empty according to their native defaults.
    Transformed-creature branch additionally appends:
        Body corrupted beyond reckoning, {he|she|it} assumes a beastly form to terrorize us.
    Call threat_details(speaker, target_historical_figure, output) at 688ef0.

The delegated call is outside the pre-existing 687db7..688ea3 sentence
inventory. Native double-space sentence separators are literal operands.

1a. Full identity construction and empty fields (688775..688dae)
-------------------------------------------------------------

Initialize an empty string and call a946e0(figure+0x38, English=true,
other-name=false) at 68879f. Append the resulting complete English name.
The shared builder's 0x140a94723..0x140a94727 tests name+0x72 (has-name);
when false it jumps directly to the epilogue at a94e6f, without a fallback
or any string write. The caller initialized length=0 at 688775..688789.
An unnamed figure therefore contributes no name text at all.

If target race differs from speaker unit+0xa4, append " the " first, then:
    valid caste with nonempty caste+0x20 name -> that singular caste string
    otherwise valid race -> race+0x20 singular RAW string
    invalid race or empty RAW names -> an empty string
The caste lookup tests actual native bounds at 68881a..6888e5. It does not
emit an invented "unknown creature" or "unnamed creature" placeholder.
The race-different branch marks that a species field was selected even when
its resulting string is empty.

Next, select exactly one of curse display title or profession/office:
    visible curse chain figure+0x130 -> +0x48, flag+0x88 != 0:
        append one space if the species field was selected, otherwise " the ";
        append the curse string at +0x90, then skip the whole office branch.
        There is no nonempty check on curse+0x90.
    no visible curse, profession enum 0x61 or 0x66:
        append no role and no additional separator.
    otherwise:
        append one space if species was selected, otherwise " the ";
        obtain a complete native profession/office title via 132cc10.
        beb620 selects gender-specific or generic RAW office strings; the
        figure/site/entity suffix is appended via 9bdfb0 when office+0x2c8>0.
        A slave reference (kind4, reference+0x10>0) overrides title to "Slave".
        A prisoner reference (kind6,+0x10>0 or other-reference kind7,+0xc>0)
        overrides title to "Prisoner", including a previous slave title.
        The native role result can be empty: the separator is already appended.
Append the period unconditionally at 688dae.

Nonempty identity productions are:
    NAME
    NAME the SPECIES
    NAME the ROLE
    NAME the SPECIES ROLE
NAME can be empty; SPECIES/ROLE can each be empty without retracting the
already emitted separator. Thus each of the four introductions above also
has real default forms PREFIX '.', PREFIX ' the .', PREFIX NAME ' the .',
and PREFIX NAME ' the SPECIES .', with their precise spaces preserved.

Stock curse fields are extracted from the configured Steam installation's
current data/vanilla, not inferred from English role names. See
vanilla-curse-fields.tsv, vanilla-curse-sources.json and the verbatim source
scripts in vanilla-curse-sources/:
    fixed CE_DISPLAY_NAME: necromancer, mummy, vampire, faded hunter
    raised undead: 33 necromancer_raise_adjectives x 8 raise singular nouns
    contagious ghouls: 6 ghoul_adjectives x 2 ghoul singular nouns
    evil-cloud zombies: 19 cloud_adjs x 9 cloud_names x 3 zombie singular nouns
    mythical powers: sphere-specific prefix/suffix adjectives, followed or
                     preceded by one of 12 rank nouns at the selected power tier
The ghost title code is present but guarded by the source's false ghost
option and false-and-ghost condition; it is not an active vanilla generator
branch. Mod-added display-name values remain RAW fields, not native fixed
English prose. The copied scripts preserve every constructor and option.

2. Crime collection and narrative
--------------------------------

65c234..65c435 walks native event collections tied to the speaker's affiliated
entities and the target historical figure. The target id is figure+0xe0.
The finite event kind branches are:
    kind 0x35: stole, target figure id is event+0x3c
    kind 0x36: destroyed a building, target figure id is event+0x28
    kind 0x37: devoured livestock, event+0x28 must be -1 and
               target figure id is event+0x34
    kind 0x45: profaned/disturbed/prayed in building, figure id event+0x2c
Other event kinds contribute no crime clause.

If at least one crime vector is nonempty, append at 65c4ea:
    Knowing no mercy, {actor} {crime_list}!

Actor is the capitalized first_name string at figure+0x38 when nonempty
(65c517..65c5e6). This branch uses only that first name. With empty first_name,
a946e0(figure+0x38, English=true) supplies a complete native figure name.
If first_name is empty and name+0x72 is false, this fallback returns without
writing: the literal "Knowing no mercy, " is followed by the additional
native actor separator space at 65c65b, yielding "Knowing no mercy,  ".

Crime categories are emitted in this fixed order, omitting absent categories:
    devoured -> stole -> destroyed -> profaned/disturbed/prayed inside
Their separators are:
    one active category:  A
    two:                  A and B
    three:                A, B and C
    four:                 A, B, C and D
There is no Oxford comma. Category count comes from native event-vector
presence, not from whether the category ultimately emits nonempty text.

devoured (65c670..65c7ad):
    vector size == 1, victim figure resolves: devoured {native_person_name}
    vector size == 1, no victim figure:       devoured a {singular_RAW_creature}
    vector size > 1:                          devoured our livestock
    absent vector:                           omitted category
The fallback uses aa3bd0(event race+0x2c, caste+0x30, plural=false).
aa3bd0 has been extracted in impact-announcement-decompiled.txt; invalid race
or an empty RAW name can yield an empty string, producing "devoured a ".
The resolved-victim branch also calls a946e0 into an initialized empty
buffer; an existing victim with has-name=false therefore emits "devoured "
without a creature fallback (65c771..65c7ad).

stole (65c7eb..65c9d0):
    vector size == 1, matching written object: stole {English_written_title}
    matching written title empty:             stole Untitled
    vector size == 1, ordinary object:         stole a {complete_item_noun}
    certain item kinds omit the inserted "a "; the finite mask is 0xa000c1
    over item_type-0x30 in range 0..0x17 (65c884..65c8ab).
    vector size > 1:                           stole our treasures
    absent vector:                            omitted category
Ordinary item construction delegates to a82c10 using event fields item kind
+0x28, subtype+0x2a, material type+0x2c, material index+0x30, artifact id+0x34.
The complete a82c10 owner is saved for both images. Its unknown-kind branch
at a88046 emits the literal "item"; written-object lookup failure falls
through to this generic noun builder, not to an empty "stole " clause.
The helper's 93 native type selectors and full underlying item description
fields are already recorded in item-description-sources.tsv. No native
lookup-failure path leaving a bare stole clause was established.

destroyed (65ca02..65cc33):
    vector size == 1 and site/building resolves:
        append "destroyed ", then named building or finite building label.
    vector size > 1: destroyed our homes
    absent vector: omitted category
    single event with missing site/building: empty category (not "destroyed")

profaned (65cc65..65cec1):
    vector size == 1 and site/building resolves:
        event action+0x28 == 0 -> "profaned"
        event action+0x28 == 1 -> "disturbed"
        event action+0x28 == 2 -> "prayed inside"
        other action -> no verb
        append " ", then named building or finite building label.
    vector size > 1: profaned our homes
    absent vector: omitted category
    single event with missing site/building: empty category

Both building-kind tables are decoded in native-switches.tsv:
    0 a mead hall; 1 a keep; 2 a temple; 3 a tower; 4 a market; 5 a tomb;
    6 dungeon subtype; 7 an underworld spire; 8 a tavern; 9 a library;
    10 a counting house; 11 a guildhall; 12 a tower; 13 a hospital.
    kind outside 0..13 -> empty label.
    dungeon subtype+0x130: 0 a dungeon; 1 the sewers; 2 the catacombs;
    other subtype -> empty label.
Named building text takes precedence over this kind switch.

Thus empty native labels after an already appended verb are real branches:
"destroyed ", "profaned ", "disturbed ", "prayed inside ". A missing action
can emit a building label with no verb. Empty categories still receive the
separator implied by their event-vector presence. A single empty category
gives "Knowing no mercy, {actor} !" before whitespace normalization.

3. Murders and kill counts
-------------------------

Known kill events are collected at 65c0b8..65c1b1 from
figure+0x130 -> +0x30 -> event ids. Anonymous counts come from that kill-info
object's race/caste/count vectors at +0x18, +0x30 and +0xa8, filtered with the
native creature-flag helper 72850(..., flag=0x3a), summed at 65c1d3..65c208.
No kill narrative is appended when both known vector and anonymous count
are zero (65cf91..65cf9c).

The subject prefix at 65d078/65d07f is:
    This vile fiend
    This bloodsucking fiend
The bloodsucking selection derives from caste flags / curse flags, including
figure+0x130 -> +0x48, and is independent of the following murder wording.

When the known event vector contains exactly one entry (65d098..65d0aa):
    This {vile|bloodsucking} fiend murdered {victim}!
    This {vile|bloodsucking} fiend even murdered {victim}!
"even " is emitted if any of the four crime vectors is nonempty. The direct
murder branch only tests the known-event vector size; an additional anonymous
kill count does not change its choice of sentence.
Victim resolves from the event's victim id at +0x28 to a historical figure.
    unrelated victim: {English_complete_person_name}
    speaker-relative victim: my {singular_family_relation} {person_name}
    missing victim figure: no victim text, yielding "murdered !" or
                           "even murdered !" before normalization
Family lookup uses bb37d0 and the relation term formatter 75a580.

With any other known-event vector size, append (65d3d2..65d5c3):
    This {vile|bloodsucking} fiend has killed {count} in {possessive} lust for murder{relatives_suffix}!
    This {vile|bloodsucking} fiend has even killed {count} in {possessive} lust for murder{relatives_suffix}!
"has even killed " is selected if any crime vector is nonempty.
count is known-vector size plus anonymous count:
    total == 1 -> somebody
    other total -> 52e360 English cardinal (hyphens and magnitude words)
Possessive follows target figure+0x6: sex 1 his; sex 0 her; other its.

65d620..65d8c3 finds killed victims in the speaker's family-id list and groups
them by family enum. If any groups exist, append:
    , among them {relative_list}
If there are none, append no relatives suffix.
Each group is:
    group count == 1 -> my {singular_family_relation}
    group count > 1  -> {English_cardinal} of my {plural_family_relation}
Multiple groups are emitted in reverse group insertion order with ", "
between earlier groups and " and " before the last; one group has no joiner.
The group count and cardinal are formatted independently of the total kills.
All 72 finite singular/plural relation selections, plus native default,
are recorded in family-relations.tsv. Wife uses wives without an additional
suffix; child-ending relation kinds and grandchild append ren; all other
kinds append s. Default is "no relationship" / "no relationships".

4. A fiend who is the speaker's relative
--------------------------------------

If the target fiend is in the speaker's family-id list (65db27..65db6d):
    [{speaker_name} pauses to regain {speaker_possessive} composure.]
    It pains me all the more, for the foul villain {is|was once} my own {relation}{curse_suffix}.
    Save us from this {horror|traitor}!

speaker_name comes from a94030(speaker unit+0x8).
speaker_possessive uses speaker unit+0x12e: 1 his; 0 her; other its.
relation uses the identified family enum, with plural=false and article=false.
Caste monster/transformation flags, curse object+0x160 or the figure's curse
byte list (+0xc8 with count +0xd0) select "was once" or "is".
curse_suffix is one of:
    , now twisted into monstrosity
    , now cursed
    empty
The same transformed/cursed state selects "horror"; ordinary relative
selects "traitor". See 65dd46..65e1ce for complete conditions.
The first sentence ends with the native sequence ".]", followed by two
spaces and the next sentence. It must remain a complete translated clause.

5. Material weakness
--------------------

65e218..65e502 selects a material pair from caste material vulnerability
records (+0x4250..+0x4258) and curse-linked alternative caste records. Compare
1000*numerator/denominator to the caste's base +0x508/+0x50c ratio; retain
the selected native material type/index. If type stays -1, emit nothing.
The vulnerability state selects one of:
    It is said that {material} harms the creature.
    Beware!  It it said that only {material} harms the creature.
The second form's native typo is exactly "It it". It also appends:
    Other arms may not cut so deeply.

Material construction 65e562..65e7b0:
    Optional historical-figure material owner: {English_person_name}'s
    Material lookup 14add70(type,index):
        material+0x520 prefix if nonempty, then a space,
        material+0xb8 name string.
    Missing material object: unknown material
The historical-material owner range is type 0xdb..0x1a2. When owner exists
but language-name valid flag+0x72 is false, the owner name is omitted while
the literal "'s " is still appended (65e657..65e6b6).
65e75f..65e78a appends material+0xb8 using its stored length, without an
explicit nonempty guard; there is no separate native empty-material branch
or fallback for a resolved material. The ordinary missing-object branch
is explicitly "unknown material" at 65e776..65e783.

6. Location lead-in
-------------------

690060 resolves site name with the shared English name builder, locates the
site or related region, then chooses these mutually exclusive lead-ins:
    current site -> We are in {site_name}.
    known direction -> {site_name} is {distance_and_direction}.
                       [You receive a detailed description.]
    region available -> {site_name} is in {region_name}.
                        region helper b94a40 includes unknown region fallback.
    region unavailable -> I've heard of a place called .

The last form is literal native control flow: 69064f appends only the prefix,
690665 capitalizes the local site-name buffer, and 690670 appends the period.
There is no append of that site-name buffer in this branch. Do not silently
infer a name placeholder from the English wording. The direction branch
uses 147c4a0, whose native distance/compass fields are already recorded in
announcement-world-fields.tsv.

With the native extra-facts flag, this owner collects eligible nearby facts
and delegates selected facts to 68d170 at 690ae9. That separate recursive
location-fact dispatcher is already represented in
announcement-description-grammar.tsv (institutions, residents, evil/blessed
places, wildlife, and complete native historical descriptions).

7. Already shared versus missing source families
-----------------------------------------------

The pre-existing announcement-rumor-grammar.tsv contains the main threat
openings, identity introductions and transformation sentence.
announcement-description-grammar.tsv contains the ordinary site-location
forms and separate extra-facts dispatcher. Neither file previously contained
the delegated 65bfb0 crime, murder, grouped family loss, related-villain or
material-vulnerability narrative. The missing location name branch above
also differs from its pre-existing inferred production.

Names, native item nouns, cardinal numbers, RAW species and material names
are delegated complete typed fields. They are not arbitrary announcement
prose slots. Source field selectors and every finite string-producing choice
in the newly missing detail owner are recorded above and in its full .asm.
